### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 47 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `867f8bb8a26fe5e434850ba0aaa0cd1e99daafad` — the merge of head `5ed7975abfba52f8ad14d088902b79711e14ef4f` into base `455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 867f8bb8a26fe5e434850ba0aaa0cd1e99daafad && git checkout 867f8bb8a26fe5e434850ba0aaa0cd1e99daafad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3 5ed7975abfba52f8ad14d088902b79711e14ef4f && git checkout -B drift-repro 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3 && git merge --no-ff 5ed7975abfba52f8ad14d088902b79711e14ef4f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5ed7975abfba52f8ad14d088902b79711e14ef4f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-crypto-provider-plugin-load-failure.integration.test.ts + packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-settings.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-detection.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/merge-boot-config.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts, packages/cli/src/index.ts, packages/cli/package.json, packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts, packages/core/src/stack-plugins.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/core/src/plugin-loader.ts, docs/adr/0116-plugin-ordering-declared-contract.md, .changeset/31007-one-shot-crypto-provider.md (precedent, read for ②)

Inputs: the PR body, its one commit, the four-path net diff from merge-base `0d0c377b` (the head sits one commit on `main` at `d3f36861e`), the check-runs on the head (32 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure; `Test Core (1/8)` and `Test Core (4/8)` still in progress when this record was rendered, nothing concluded red), and the drafter's private hand-back, whose claims were checked against the tree. No card, by the maintainer's ruling for this series; #28284 is the series mailbox and carries nothing on this PR.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `os serve` (`@objectstack/cli`), narrowed on exactly two shapes.** After the stack-plugin loop in `run()` (`serve.ts` 4719-4765 on the head) and before the host crypto provider is built (5125), `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins` (6443) throws `HostCryptoProviderRefusal` for every entry the loop could not load that is (a) a string specifier that never materialized, or (b) an entry that materialized to, or is itself, an object whose `providesServices` names `'crypto-provider'`. The throw escapes to `run()`'s outer catch (6078), which prints the message and exits 1; the integration pin shows the refusal line and no bound port. **Right**: the published provider contract on `main` (`packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts`) says a provider plugin declares the service in `providesServices`, and the one-shot secret commands on `main` (`one-shot-settings.ts`, `readDeclaredCryptoProvider`) already refuse the same two shapes over the same host config. This is that rule applied to the long-lived host.
- **Entries that declare other services, or none, keep the old handling** (printed `✗ Failed to load plugin`, boot goes on). **Right against the contract**, which is declaration-based (the same reading `cryptoProviderPlugins` takes on `main`), but the new docstring says otherwise (see ④, should-fix 1).
- **Postures.** The check sits unconditionally in `run()`, so it holds in production and under `--dev`; `stackBootPlugins` appends `devPlugins` after `plugins` under `--dev`, so they are covered; `os start` spawns a `serve` child (`start.ts`) and so shares it. **Right**, with one labelling caveat (④, should-fix 2).
- **Public surface: unchanged.** The two new named exports (`refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins`, `UnloadedStackPlugin`) sit in `commands/serve.ts`; the package's export map reaches only `dist/index.js`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports only the default `ServeCommand`. Nothing new is reachable from `@objectstack/cli`. **Right.**
- **Refusal text.** Names each refused entry as `plugins[i] ('specifier or name')` with the load error, lists only refused entries (ruled-out ones are not named), and carries no registered value. **Right** (unit pin `expectNoKeyMaterial`).
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`.** Nothing a metadata author writes changes. **Right.**
- **Order of events.** Record in the loop's catch (4761) precedes the check (4767), which precedes provider construction (5125); the unit source-pin holds the three strings, all present on the head at those lines. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset**: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, a bug fix in a released package; correct level, and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
- **`Clause-②: no` is correct, not `no (narrowing)`.** The question is whether a published package's accept set or public surface is narrowed. The surface is unchanged (①). The configs now refused are the two shapes the published provider contract on `main` already refuses for the same host config in the one-shot secret commands; the long-lived host was the one consumer still booting them after printing a load error. That is the spec's own refusal made real at the remaining consumer, not a declared capability taken away: no public doc on `main` promises that `os serve` goes on after a `plugins` entry fails to load (`content/docs` searched), and nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no FROM-to-TO migration exists to carry. Precedent: #31228 (`.changeset/31007-one-shot-crypto-provider.md`, merged) refused previously-succeeding one-shot runs on the same configs and declared `Clause-②: no` at `patch`. Both declaration lines are present and identical in the PR body and the changeset.
- **Disclosure check** (PR body, commit message, changeset, new source comments and test headers): every sentence stays at the level of behaviour and of the provider contract `main` already publishes in `packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts` and `serve.ts`'s existing comments; the why line is the maintainer's fixed one, 「QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)」. No breach found.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Hand-back findings 1 and 2 (pre-existing, outside this PR's narrowing).** Both confirmed in the tree; neither is a gap this PR opens or claims to cover. **Escalated**: each becomes its own private item in this series; details stay off GitHub under the disclosure ruling.
2. **Hand-back finding 3 (a provider plugin that loads but whose `init()` fails).** **Answered, closed**: the boot exits 1. No gap.
3. **Hand-back finding 4 (overlap with #31228).** Resolved as stated; but the PR landed second and did not adopt the shared reading (④, should-fix 3).
4. **`os start` not measured.** **Answered, closed**: `start.ts` spawns the `serve` child; same `run()`, same check.
5. **Caller-class matrix n/a.** Agreed: a boot-time host decision with no request caller.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the spec on `main`: it does not take a declared capability away at the consumer. The capability the author declares is the plugin; the behaviour removed is the host's own leniency after it had already rejected that plugin with an error line, a leniency no published doc declares and one the published provider contract and the one-shot rule on `main` already refuse. The design holds; three should-fixes, no must-fix.

Break attempts, each against the live tree: six shapes of an entry failing to load, or being dropped, between the stack loop and the provider construction. None defeats the check within this PR's scope; the detail is in the seat's private notes, under the disclosure ruling.

Findings:
1. **Should-fix: the docstring states a stricter rule than the code applies.** `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins`'s comment says an entry is ruled out "only by what it says it provides: ... has a `providesServices` (ADR-0116) that does not name the provider", and the PR body says the same; the code and the CONTROL pin also rule out a materialized object with no `providesServices` at all, as the commit message says ("or none"). The code is the contract-consistent reading; make the docstring and the PR body say it plainly ("declares other services, or declares none, is ruled out").
2. **Should-fix: label a `devPlugins` entry as such.** Under `--dev` the index is a position in the merged list, so a `devPlugins[j]` entry is named `plugins[plugins.length + j]`. Record the source list in `UnloadedStackPlugin` (or offset the index) so the refusal names where the entry actually sits; the name in parentheses keeps it findable meanwhile.
3. **Should-fix: one reading of the declaration.** The new function restates the `providesServices` predicate that `cryptoProviderPlugins` (6382) already is, which `one-shot-settings.ts` names as "the one reading" `serve` and the one-shot commands share. Route the ruling-out through that predicate so the two cannot drift.
